newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- watching CPI, Tues. deals.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- watching CPI, Tues. deals.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds were unchanged in extremely quiet action Monday, as traders said they were hoping Tuesday's economic data and new deals would offer direction.
"It was like a Saturday," one trader said of Monday's activity levels.
Market participants said there were many bid-wanted lists circulating during the day, but the dollar totals were not substantial.
The government market was likewise little changed heading into the New York close. The long bond was off 1/32 at 93-10/32 to yield 7.17 percent.

In debt futures, the June municipal contract closed up 5/32 at 111-25/32 and the June T-bond contract was up 2/32 at 106-22/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts widened to 163 ticks from 160 at the close on Friday.

In the secondary market, bids on Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were unchanged from Friday at 96-1/4. North Carolina Medical Care Commission MBIA 5-3/8s of 2026 were also unchanged, at 5.98 percent.
Monday's trading activity was light ahead of Tuesday's new supply and release of another inflation yardstick, the Consumer Price Index for March.
Economists in a Reuters poll predicted the CPI would show a 0.2 percent rise, with the figure excluding food and energy seen gaining 0.3 percent.
Municipal bond sales for Tuesday are expected to total $439 million in 45 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $182 million in seven sales, with a $98 million Port of Corpus Christi, Texas, deal through Lehman Brothers topping the list.
On the competitive side, 38 sales totaling $257 million are on the schedule. A $70 million Clark County, Nev., deal at 1100 EDT is the largest.
